Multivariate LOESS

Source: vignettes/dimensions.Rmd
dimensions.Rmd

Overview

Standard LOESS operates on a single predictor x. LOESS extends this to an n-dimensional predictor space by passing a matrix as x, enabling surface smoothing over spatial grids, time–altitude combinations, and similar multi-predictor datasets.

Dimensions Use Case x Input Shape
1 Time series, 1D signal (default) Numeric vector
2 Spatial surface, 2-predictor model n × 2 matrix
3+ High-dimensional regression n × d matrix

Note: Neighbourhood search scales with the number of dimensions. For d ≥ 3 keep fraction small and consider the "interpolation" surface mode (the default) to reduce computation.

1D — Standard (Default)

Single predictor. No configuration required.

library(rfastloess)
set.seed(42)
x <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 200)
y <- sin(x) + rnorm(200, sd = 0.2)

model <- Loess(fraction = 0.3)
result <- fit(model, x, y)

2D — Spatial Surface

Two predictors (e.g., latitude/longitude, time/altitude). Pass an n × 2 matrix as x.

set.seed(42)
n <- 100
lat <- runif(n, -pi, pi)
lon <- runif(n, -pi, pi)
z   <- sin(lat) + cos(lon) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.1)

x2d <- cbind(lat, lon)   # n × 2 matrix

model <- Loess(fraction = 0.3)
result <- fit(model, x2d, z)

3D and Higher

Pass an n × d matrix as x. Higher dimensions require a larger fraction to keep the local neighbourhood populated.

set.seed(42)
n <- 200
x1 <- runif(n)
x2 <- runif(n)
x3 <- runif(n)
y  <- x1 + sin(2 * pi * x2) + x3^2 + rnorm(n, sd = 0.1)

x3d <- cbind(x1, x2, x3)   # n × 3 matrix

model <- Loess(fraction = 0.5)
result <- fit(model, x3d, y)

Distance Metrics

In multivariate mode, neighbour distances can be computed with different metrics.

Metric Description When to Use
"normalized" Each dimension scaled by its range (default) Mixed-scale predictors
"euclidean" Raw Euclidean distance Same-scale predictors
"weighted" Per-dimension scaling via weighted_metric_weights Custom anisotropic distance 
# Upweight time dimension relative to spatial dimension
x2d <- cbind(time_col, space_col)

model <- Loess(
    fraction = 0.3,
    distance_metric = "weighted",
    weighted_metric_weights = c(2.0, 1.0)  # time counts twice
)
result <- fit(model, x2d, y)

Surface Mode

Mode Behaviour Speed
"interpolation" Fit at grid vertices, interpolate elsewhere (default) Fast
"direct" Fit directly at every query point Exact, slower 
# Exact fit at every point — slower but no interpolation artefacts
model <- Loess(surface_mode = "direct", fraction = 0.3)
result <- fit(model, x2d, z)

For large 2D or 3D datasets use "interpolation" (default) and tune cell and interpolation_vertices to control grid resolution.

model <- Loess(
    surface_mode = "interpolation",
    cell = 0.2,
    interpolation_vertices = 200L,
    fraction = 0.3
)
result <- fit(model, x2d, z)
